output.title: Letter to Governor-General Willem Arnold Alting regarding English Ship Atlas
output.abstract: Official correspondence addressed to Governor-General Willem Arnold Alting in Batavia from the Council of Netherlands India. The document references a duplicate letter sent via the English ship 'Atlas'. Alting served as Governor-General of the Dutch East Indies (1780-1796), and this communication appears to concern maritime correspondence procedures between VOC officials, utilizing an English vessel as a carrier for official Dutch colonial dispatches.

output.title: VOC Financial Management: Ceylon Monetary Demands and Credit Policies, 1785
output.abstract: This document discusses the VOC's financial challenges in Ceylon, emphasizing careful management of monetary demands due to limited local credit opportunities. Key topics include the introduction of paper money and its limitations, increased interest rates to 9%, copper coinage issues, and distribution of goods among VOC chambers (Rotterdam and Amsterdam). The text addresses a request for financial support of 13,000 guilders for 1785 and coordination with Cape officials regarding monetary policies and their impact on both Company and private trade.

output.title: VOC Financial Crisis and Request for Relief from Sovereign, ca. 1780s
output.abstract: This document describes the VOC's severe financial difficulties and emergency measures taken to address them. The Company awaits a decision from the sovereign regarding their petition for relief. Commissioners are tasked with distributing undivided Indian and Cape goods among the respective chambers during the upcoming June meeting in The Hague. Chambers are requested to send allocated funds to India or the Cape at the earliest opportunity. The text reflects the Company's desperate financial situation and dependence on governmental intervention.

output.title: Extract from VOC Letter: Cape to Batavia via Amsterdam, November 1784
output.abstract: Extract from a November 18, 1784 letter sent by the VOC Seventeen (Heeren XVII) to the Governor-General and Council of the Indies in Batavia. References previous correspondence from May 15 and August 6, 1784. Details the problematic transport of letters and papers from the Cape of Good Hope via the Company logger ship De Zwaluw, which had to put in at Padang due to poor condition and was sold as irreparable. Consequently, documents were sent overland from Spain to Amsterdam instead.

output.title: VOC Ceylon Rice Supply and Chank Shell Diving Contract Disputes, 1778-1784
output.abstract: This document discusses a proposal to supply 800-1000 lasts of Bengali or Coromandel rice annually to Ceylon, to be paid in chank shells (sjankoosen). The VOC suspended chank diving farm leases in favor of direct Company operations. A significant dispute concerns unpaid chank shells from 1778-1779 involving Bengali merchant Blinne and former Director Ross, complicated by the English capture of Trincomalee. The Gentlemen XVII (Hunne Hoog Edelheeden) ordered recovery of debts but acknowledged wartime difficulties. The document references correspondence from June 1780 through September 1784.

output.title: VOC Resolution on Linen Tax Farm Arrears in Colombo, 1781-1782
output.abstract: This document discusses a VOC resolution from January 15, 1782, regarding compensation for a tax farmer (pachter) of linen cloth (lijwaad) in Colombo, Galle, and Kalpettij. Due to wartime conditions and reduced trade, the farmer's payment obligation was reduced from 16,080 rixdollars to 7,250.36¾ rixdollars, representing actual revenues collected after deducting unavoidable expenses. The text also addresses arrears from previous linen tax farmers (1776-1780) in Colombo, criticizing lenient collection practices based on farmers' unverified claims of inability to convert merchandise to cash.

output.title: VOC Resolution on Secretaries' Widow Compensation and Tax Arrears, 1782
output.abstract: This document concerns a 1782 VOC resolution regarding compensation for widows of secretaries Lebeck and others who served in Palembang. It addresses the collection of the 'twintigste penning' (twentieth penny tax) for the years 1775-1776, which remained unpaid to the Company. The High Government orders local officials to settle these arrears and hold responsible parties accountable for the delays. The text discusses the tension between compensating widows and ensuring the Company suffers no financial loss due to officials' negligence in tax collection.

output.title: VOC Report on the Fall of Trincomalee Fortress, 1782
output.abstract: This document discusses the Dutch East India Company's concerns regarding the fate of Trincomalee fortress in 1782. It references secret correspondence from April and June 1782 regarding the incomplete state of fortifications and defenses. The text criticizes the defective, confused, and imprudent manner of defense, noting that landward fortifications were inadequate when the fort fell to the enemy. The document mentions Ridder Des Roijs and evaluates the Company's defensive preparations during this critical period of the Fourth Anglo-Dutch War.

output.title: VOC Orders Regarding Ships and War with England, December 1781
output.abstract: This document discusses VOC deliberations during wartime with England regarding the fate of company ships and their cargo. Officials debate whether vessels should be destroyed rather than captured by the English if safe passage cannot be secured. References are made to secret correspondence from February 12 concerning Trincomalee (Ceylon), two chaloupes at Pale, and English frigates observed between December 5-24, 1781. The text reflects strategic decisions about protecting VOC assets during Anglo-Dutch hostilities.

output.title: Investigation of Smuggling Allegations Involving Skipper Jansen (VOC)
output.abstract: This document discusses an investigation into suspected smuggling activities involving skipper Jansen and the captain of an English vessel anchored in Paalsche Bay. The investigation was hindered by Jansen's death, preventing his testimony. The text criticizes attempts by a warehouse master (Pakhuijsmeester) to deflect blame onto others rather than properly account for his own conduct, noting that such diversionary tactics only increased suspicions against him. The passage reflects VOC procedures for investigating illicit trade and accountability of company officials.

output.title: VOC Ship Spaarenrijk Operations: Pepper and Rice Trade Routes, 1700s
output.abstract: Resolution dated October 11 documenting the VOC ship Spaarenrijk's trading activities between Ceylon (Sri Lanka), Cochin (Koetsjim), and Porca. The vessel transported goods from the ship De Bodt, departed November 20 for Cochin to load pepper and rice cargo. Communication delays prompted duplicate correspondence dated December 30. The bark De Liefde brought news that Spaarenrijk had been sent to Porca for pepper collection on the 23rd, with the ship's commander reporting from Gale that Spaarenrijk departed Porca on the first of the month returning to Ceylon.

output.title: VOC Decision to Reassign Ship Stavenisse from Zeeland to Amsterdam Chamber
output.abstract: This document records a VOC meeting decision from the 24th of the month regarding the ship Stavenisse. Originally consigned to the Zeeland Chamber and destined for Ceylon, the ship missed its voyage. The Amsterdam Presidial Chamber decided to reassign Stavenisse to Amsterdam instead, as they lacked sufficient pepper and saltpeter to load two return ships. Instructions were given to Paalse officials to load the Stavenisse with proper ballast including saltpeter.

output.title: VOC Ships Stavenisse and Middelwijk: Cargo Reports and Voyages, 1760s
output.abstract: This document records the arrivals and departures of VOC ships Stavenisse and Middelwijk between October and December. The Stavenisse, originally designated as a return ship to the Netherlands for the Zeeland chamber but reassigned to Amsterdam, arrived from Batavia on October 10th. It subsequently made a voyage to Koesjiem (Cochin) and Gale (Galle) carrying rice, pepper, and supplies for the squadron. The Middelwijk arrived later on October 19th despite departing Batavia earlier. Both ships' cargoes were partially unloaded and redistributed according to resolutions.

output.title: VOC Horse Breeding on Delft Island and Textile Trade Regulations, 1700s
output.abstract: This VOC document details horse breeding operations on Delft Island and Twee Gebroeders, listing 3 Persian stallions, 7 indigenous horses, 119 adult mares, and various foals, with maintenance costs of 817 guilders. The text also addresses textile (lijwaaten) procurement policies, including a resolution from March 19th and April 4th regarding the resumption of cloth collection from the Madurai coast. It mentions the prohibition of certain coarse Madurai textiles and price adjustments, alongside the sale of two unusable horses via public auction.

output.title: Chank Diving Lease and Contract with Count of Bijland, Ceylon 1750
output.abstract: This VOC document discusses the chank (conch shell) diving operations along Ceylon's coasts and Tuticorin. A general lease auction yielded only 3,600 and 1,850 rixdollars respectively, far below expected value. The resolution of September 3rd decided to maintain operations under Company account to fulfill contractual obligations with the Count of Bijland, dated June 24-30. The agreement involved either accepting the Count's proposed contract terms for chanks dived on Company account, or alternatively supplying 800 lasten of rice as payment.

output.title: VOC Chank Shell Diving Operations at Kalpitiya and Aripo Banks, 1786
output.abstract: This document records VOC administrative decisions regarding chank shell (sjankos) diving operations at Kalpitiya and the Aripo Banks along Ceylon's coast. Key resolutions from October 22 and December 29 detail payment rates to divers (16:32 rixdollars for quantities exceeding 20,000 shells). The text mentions an inspection of the Aripo Banks on August 26 by commissioners including dessave De Bock and Jaffnapatnam administrator de Lannoij. References are made to rice prices (4 ropias per sack) and a burgher named Blinne's unfulfilled request regarding 1786 shell contracts.

output.title: Pearl Bank Inspection Report - Tutucorijn, Kalpettij, and Madurai Coast
output.abstract: Report on unsuccessful pearl oyster inspections conducted at Tutucorijn and Kalpettij banks by VOC officials including Captain Commandant of Kalpettij Kusen and merchant van Rantzouw. Despite high expectations and thorough efforts, commissioners found very few and immature pearl oysters. Resolution of December 29 noted the findings for reporting to High Authorities. Additionally records decision of November 22 to inspect pearl banks on the Madurai coast at the insistence of Nabob Machmiet Alichan, with results pending.

output.title: VOC Padang: Purchase of Trade Goods and Provisions, 1776
output.abstract: This document details the VOC's procurement of trade goods and provisions in Padang throughout the year, as necessitated by warehouse shortages. Notable transactions include the emergency purchase of 6,000 sacks of Bengali rice (150 lb each at 6 rupees per sack) from the English ship 'Stasting' arriving from Bengal in March, due to severe rice shortages. Additional purchases of Dutch provisions including rope, sailcloth, sail yarn, pitch, tar, and hemp were made in Padang and Pulu (Pale) to supply the Dutch squadron's urgent needs.

output.title: VOC Spice Trade and Dutch Commodities Price List with Profit Margins
output.abstract: A detailed VOC accounting document listing purchase and sale prices for spices (specerijen) including nutmeg (noten musshaeten), mace (foelie), cinnamon (kanneel), and cloves (tarioffel nagulen), alongside various Dutch commodities (Vaderlandsche Koopmanschappen). The document records quantities in pounds (lb), purchase prices (inkoop), selling prices (verkoops), and profit percentages. Additional items include beer, tools, copper, silver, glass, textiles, sailcloth, books, and camphor. Total values exceed 60,000 guilders, demonstrating the scale of VOC commercial operations and profit calculations.

output.title: VOC Inventory and Valuation of Trade Goods and Supplies
output.abstract: A detailed financial inventory listing VOC trade commodities and supplies with purchase and sale prices. Items include Surat tarwa, Coromandel textiles (patti, Guinea cloth, salempores), medicinal goods (opium, cassia beans, mustard seed), Japanese copper bars, Javanese rice and rattans, Ceylonese coffee and pepper, sugar candy, double arrack, tamarind, and ship supplies. The document records quantities in various units (lasten, ponden, kannen) with corresponding values in guilders, showing both acquisition costs (inkoops) and sales profits (verkoops winst). Total values exceed 230,000 guilders, representing significant VOC commercial operations across Asian trading posts.

output.title: VOC Council Resolution on Spice Prices and Domain Revenues, 1784-1786
output.abstract: This document records resolutions from the VOC Council of the Indies regarding spice trade regulations and colonial revenues. Key decisions include setting prices for nutmeg at 100 Indian guilders and mace at 150 stuivers (July 1784, June 1785). It reports an accounting error in clove sales quantities for 1783/84 and details domain revenue increases from tax farms, rising from ƒ283,801 to ƒ397,429 in 1785/86. The salt transport ban to the uplands caused difficulties in leasing Putelang tax farms, requiring monthly collection arrangements instead.

output.title: VOC Domain Leases in Jaffna and Mannar, August-September 1700s
output.abstract: Records the public auctioning of VOC company domains in Jaffna and Mannar on August 26-27, including the Ponnorijn to Pringalij lease for 585 rixdollars. Textile leases in Colombo, Galle, and Kalpitiya were held until September 3, fetching 20,000 rixdollars. Documents preferential bidding procedures for certain lessees and approved rent reductions: 150 rixdollars for the Levai salt pans lessee due to losses from salt transport restrictions, and 2,000 rixdollars for Jaffna lessees of inland cloth shops and passage rights at Colombo-Gamme.

output.title: VOC Pagoda Mint Production Report Colombo, September 1784-August 1785
output.abstract: Financial report from the VOC pagoda mint in Colombo documenting the production of 101,759 pagodas (gold coins) from 1,413 marks of fine gold between September 1784 and August 1785. The document details the receipt of 25 bhaars of gold from Europe via the Cape of Good Hope, originally shipped on the vessel 'Les Six Frères' and transferred via the frigate 'De Waakzaamheid' to Galle, then overland to Colombo. Each bhaar is numbered and weighed at approximately 18 kant with 5½ prijn fineness, representing Chamber Zeeland's gold supply for colonial minting operations.

output.title: VOC Gold Shipment Inventory from Batavia and Zeeland (18th Century)
output.abstract: Detailed inventory of gold bars (bhaeren) transported to VOC headquarters via multiple ships. Records 82 gold bars and fragments shipped from Batavia aboard the Triton (14 bars) and from Zeeland aboard the Stavenisse (68 bars). Each entry documents bar number, weight, and gold purity assay (gessaieert) ranging from 18-21 carats. The systematic numbering and quality assessment reflects VOC's meticulous commodity tracking procedures for precious metal shipments between colonial territories and the Netherlands.

output.title: VOC Gold Pagoda Minting Operations and Assay Records, Third Batch
output.abstract: Detailed accounting of gold pagoda coin minting operations, documenting the processing of 102,164+ pagodas through multiple batches. Records include assay results at 18¼ carats, addition of Japanese refined copper to achieve proper alloy standards, weight losses during smelting and striking, and distribution of coins to the Chief Administrator's treasury. Documents costs for materials, labor (silversmiths, minters, writers, smelters), and supplies (oil, pots, lemons, tamarind). Includes verification by the fiscal and council members, with detailed calculations of fine marks at 375 guilders per mark and final valuations exceeding 252,000 guilders.

output.title: VOC Coinage Operations and Gold Minting Records at Tuticorin Mint
output.abstract: This document records multiple gold minting operations (vermunting) at the VOC mint in Tuticorin, detailing five separate batches with precise weights in marks, karats, and grains. Total receipts reached ƒ408,595, with 101,759 pagodas coined for the Company, yielding a profit of approximately 3.3% or ƒ13,705. The text also mentions the mint's temporary closure the previous year and plans to relocate it from the government premises back to Tuticorin, as per resolutions from April and November. Additionally, worn silverware from government stock was melted down for recoining.

output.title: Commission Report on Colombo Fortification Works, March 1786
output.abstract: A resolution from March 3, 1786, appointed a commission led by Major Paravicini to assess the fortification works at Colombo, similar to work done at Galle (Pale). The report's completion was delayed due to Paravicini's absence in Trincomalee. The document discusses the current state of defensive works and necessary improvements, intended for review by the VOC Directors (Heeren Meesteren). Reference is made to the ship Stavenisse and work conducted by the fleet in Galle Bay, with hopes to provide at least a preliminary report.

output.title: Instructions for VOC Engineer Lieutenant Lawe on Fortification Works
output.abstract: This document outlines regulations for Lieutenant Lawe, a VOC engineer, regarding fortification construction projects. It mandates continuous work on three defensive installations to prepare them against enemy attack. Lawe must take an annual oath concerning his faithful conduct in managing coolies, servants, and craftsmen, as well as all matters under his engineering department. The text emphasizes strict punishment for any unfaithful behavior, demonstrating VOC oversight of military infrastructure and labor management in colonial territories.

output.title: Request for Salary Increase for Lieutenant Lowe and VOC Construction Costs
output.abstract: A petition to the VOC authorities requesting an annual allowance of 1800 ropijen (150 ropijen monthly) for Lieutenant Lowe, arguing that adequate compensation enables servants to fulfill their duties without resorting to illicit means. The document includes detailed construction and repair costs totaling ƒ56,898.10 across VOC establishments including Colombo (ƒ41,874.13.8), Gale (ƒ11,558.4.8), Jaffanapatnam (ƒ2,160.4), Mannar (ƒ909.13.8), and Mature (ƒ395.14.2), demonstrating significant infrastructure expenses in Ceylon.

output.title: Administrative Reports and Confrontations at Colombo and Jaffnapatnam, 1784
output.abstract: This document records quarterly administrative reports and inventory confrontations (audits) conducted at VOC establishments in Colombo and Jaffnapatnam in 1784. Key items include the apothecary's quarterly reports on prepared medications, confrontations of workshops and iron magazines completed by August 1784, verification of accounts against negotiation books, compensation for iron work at the ammunition house, and write-offs of defective goods from the material warehouse. Resolutions are dated throughout 1784, demonstrating routine VOC administrative oversight in Ceylon.

output.title: Dismissal and Audit of Agent Zeeke at Tranquebar, 1784-1785
output.abstract: Administrative correspondence regarding the dismissal and financial accounting of Agent Zeeke (or Geeke) stationed at Tranquebar. Documents his recall to Colombo in January 1785 for final settlement of accounts covering August 1784 through January 1785. References disputes requiring resolution between Zeeke and Captain-Lieutenant De Bellon, who commanded sepoys on the Coromandel Coast. Includes mention of warehouse inventory findings at Pale (Gale) from August 1784 and resolutions dated February 1 and April 4, with reports from visitateur Berghuijs.

output.title: VOC General Accounts and Expenses Report 1784-1785
output.abstract: Financial overview of VOC operations comparing fiscal years 1784 and 1785, detailing general profits (ƒ643,770) and expenses (ƒ1,503,564) in Dutch guilders. Documents audited salary books from Colombo, Jaffanapatnam, and Palo, along with muster rolls of indigenous military personnel. Reports inventory of cash, merchandise, provisions, equipment and ammunition totaling ƒ6,126,694 as of August 1785, showing an increase from the previous year. Includes references to management memoranda and administrative orders from July 1780.

output.title: VOC Ceylon Salary Records and Requisition of Supplies (1700s)
output.abstract: Administrative document from VOC Ceylon (Sri Lanka) detailing salary payments to Coromandel servants recorded in Ceylon payroll books, and payments to bookkeepers and medical visitors transferred from Nagapatnam to Colombo. References resolutions from February, March, May, and December regarding payment specifications. Includes a formal requisition (eijsch) of needed supplies submitted to higher authorities, with references to administrative decisions of minor importance from May 7 and 31.

output.title: VOC Inventory List of Trade Goods and Supplies, January 1786
output.abstract: A detailed inventory from January 1786 listing VOC trade commodities and supplies with quantities. Major items include 300,000 lb sugar, 100,000 lb Japanese copper, spices (nutmeg, cloves, mace), tin, pewter, Chinese porcelain (plates, bowls, dishes), Nanking linen, rice (1,600 lasten), wax candles, arrack, and military supplies (gunflints, drum strings). The document reflects typical VOC trade goods between Asia and the Dutch Republic, including both luxury items and essential provisions for colonial administration.

output.title: VOC Supply Requisition List for Workshops, Pharmacy, and Shipyards
output.abstract: This VOC document details supply requisitions for various workshops and facilities, including timber yards (Timmerwerven), the pharmacy (Medicijn winkel), and smiths' and coopers' workshops. Medical supplies listed include radix China, camphor, calumba root, ipecacuanha, sassafras wood, and various oils. Construction materials specify timber dimensions in feet (voet) and duim for shipyard work, carriage makers, and general carpentry. The document includes quantities of Venetian borax, barrel staves, and various wooden beams. It appears to be a five-year supply forecast (vijff Jaeren) with detailed measurements and allocations across different VOC operational departments.

output.title: VOC Ceylon Financial Overview: Cash, Rice, and Supplies Inventory 1782
output.abstract: Inventory and financial statement from VOC Ceylon (Sri Lanka) dated 1782, detailing supplies for shipbuilding and carpentry workshops including various sizes of tin cans, tools, and materials. Lists cash reserves and provisions (rice, nelie/oil) across multiple VOC stations: Colombo (ƒ280,634), Jaffna, Mannar, Galle, Matara, Trincomalee, Batticaloa, and Kalpitiya. Document includes duration calculations for supply reserves and monetary accounts for each residency, providing insight into VOC operational logistics and resource distribution across Ceylon's coastal settlements.

output.title: Dispute Between Justice Council and Orphan Masters at Batavia Castle, 1700s
output.abstract: This VOC document addresses a complaint from the Council of Justice at Batavia Castle regarding orphan masters (weesmeesters) who failed to comply with a judicial ruling. The Justice Council requested clarification on their authority to use coercive measures (contrainte) against non-compliant orphan masters. In a resolution dated September 3, the VOC authorities affirmed that the orphan chamber and other administrative colleges must submit to Justice Council rulings and can be prosecuted through execution without exception. The orphan masters were subsequently instructed on their duties.

output.title: VOC Report on Seminary Education and Teacher Training Deficiencies
output.abstract: This document discusses concerns about a VOC-established educational institution (seminary/Seminarium), referencing resolutions from April 15 and September 6. The text criticizes the quality of teachers and notes that students sent to the Netherlands had to return to lower classes, indicating inadequate training. The report emphasizes that despite significant Company expenses, the institution requires better qualified instructors than locally available to properly train catechism masters and indigenous schoolmasters. The document appears to be addressed to high authorities (Hoog Edelheden) regarding educational reform proposals.

output.title: Jaffna Orphan Masters' Proposal for Widow and Orphan Support, 1784-1785
output.abstract: The orphan masters (weesmeesteren) of Jaffna submitted a request to support European widows and orphans from surplus interest funds. They reported that many widows and orphans of European descent were inadequately maintained by the Deacons or not at all. With accumulated interest of 1117 rijksdaalders and 3 stuivers as of August 1784, they proposed distributions without diminishing the capital fund. The VOC authorities approved this proposal on May 7, commending the orphan masters' paternal care and establishing a fund to compensate for any losses to pupil funds.

output.title: Financial Records of Diaconate and Leper House in Ceylon, 1700s
output.abstract: Financial accounting of the Diaconate (Diaconij) capital across VOC Ceylon establishments, totaling ƒ126,161.14.4½, distributed among Colombo (ƒ36,882), Jaffna and Mannar (ƒ58,185), Galle and Matara (ƒ22,486), and Kalpitiya (ƒ8,612). Documents repairs to the dilapidated Leper House (Leproosen huijs) authorized by resolution of September 13, costing 1,709 rixdollars, charged to the Leper House fund which held ƒ31,735 as of late August. Includes references to resolutions dated the 16th of the month.

output.title: VOC Correspondence on Tuticorin Pearl Fishery Dispute with the Nabab, 1780s
output.abstract: This document records correspondence between VOC officials and the Nabab regarding disputes over pearl fishery operations at Tuticorin. Key events include the arrival of the Nabab's commissioners to inspect the pearl banks, and the dispatch of an English doctor named Dot as negotiator. References are made to resolutions from September 22, November 7, and December 12, with multiple letters exchanged between the Governor, the Nabab, and Tuticorin officials. The matter concerns visitation rights and regulatory control over the lucrative Tuticorin pearl banks.

output.title: VOC Regulation on Honorary Titles (Don/Modliaar) in Jaffna, 1760 onwards
output.abstract: This document outlines VOC regulations regarding the granting and renewal of honorary titles 'Don' or 'Modliaar' in Jaffna. Individuals who received these titles provisionally from commanders since 1760 must renew their certificates within six weeks, paying 12 rijksdaalders for the seal plus half a rijksdaalder in secretarial fees. New applicants pay the same seal fee, half rijksdaalder expedition costs, and additional fees to the Commander, not exceeding 25 rijksdaalders total. The regulation emphasizes these titles cause no inconvenience to Company service and participation is voluntary.

output.title: Appointment of Thomas Nagel as Administrator of Vanni Lands, Jaffanapatam
output.abstract: This document justifies the appointment of artillery lieutenant and sworn surveyor Thomas Nagel to administer newly acquired Vanni lands under direct VOC control in Jaffanapatam, Ceylon. It credits Nagel with creating the initial proposal for bringing these territories under Company rule and successfully suppressing a dangerous rebellion. His sixteen years of experience as surveyor in Jaffanapatam provided extensive knowledge of the land and people. The text emphasizes the necessity of assigning him appropriate authority given the known character of the Ceylonese population.

output.title: VOC Request for Supplies from French Governor Coutancheau at Pondicherry
output.abstract: This document records negotiations between VOC officials and French Governor Coutancheau at Pondicherry regarding the supply of needed goods, particularly ammunition. The French Governor agreed to provide the necessary supplies but could not establish prices immediately, proposing instead to deliver goods against receipt with final settlement to be determined between the respective governments in Europe. The VOC accepted this arrangement and received ammunition supplies from the French government on receipt.

output.title: Discharge of Artillery Captain-Lieutenant Heupner as Armory Overseer (1780s)
output.abstract: Administrative record documenting the discharge of Captain-Lieutenant Klaas Ditloff Heupner from his position as overseer of the VOC company armory due to advanced age and increasing physical ailments. The document references correspondence with the Heeren XVII (Lords Seventeen) regarding received ammunition goods and settlement accounts with the French Government. Heupner was permitted to continue serving as captain of artillery while being relieved of his armory oversight duties.

output.title: Arrest and Resistance Against VOC Governor Authority
output.abstract: This document discusses tensions between VOC officials and a willful, embittered chief who has the power to arrest subordinates at any moment. It references Colonel D'Hugonet and growing unrest due to news of conflicts between the Republic and the Emperor. The text highlights an arrested individual's clear intention to resist the Government, as detailed in a report from the fiscal to the Zeeland Chamber directors. The author warns of serious consequences if decisive action is delayed.

output.title: VOC Ceylon: Judicial Proceedings and Conflicts with Luxembourg Regiment
output.abstract: This document addresses serious disciplinary issues with the Luxembourg Regiment stationed in Ceylon. The fiscal has been ordered to prosecute arrested soldiers and their accomplices according to legal procedures. The case has become a judicial matter to be decided by the High Authorities. The text details ongoing daily difficulties with the Luxembourg Regiment and references correspondence to the Zeeland Chamber directors. It emphasizes the dangerous situation of having a large military force without proper subordination and control, noting that command over the regiment was provisionally assigned by resolution of September 13th.

output.title: Financial Arrangements for the Luxembourg Regiment in VOC Service
output.abstract: This document details financial and supply arrangements for the Luxembourg Regiment serving under VOC command. Key provisions include: payment adjustments of five stuivers per guilder, equalization of Luxembourg soldiers' treatment with other Company troops per capitulation terms, provision of nanking linen and other fabrics from Company warehouses for uniforms at standard prices, and supply of weapons (snaphaanen) to recruits arriving with Colonel D'Hilgonet. Expenses for weapons and repairs are charged to the regiment on separate accounts, with annual settlements sent to the Zeeland Chamber directors, as the Prince of Luxembourg bears these costs per capitulation agreement.

output.title: VOC Military Personnel Roster: Soldiers, Musketeers, and Sailors at Trincomalee
output.abstract: A detailed muster roll listing VOC military personnel stationed at Trincomalee (Tinkonomale), including 2 soldiers, 6 musketeers, 1 drummer (tambour), 22 sailors (matrozen), and 1 Eastern soldier. The roster documents names and places of origin spanning Europe and Asia, including recruits from Dutch cities (Amsterdam, Leiden), German territories (Königsberg, Kleef), French locations (Marseille, Dunkirk), and Asian ports (Malakka, Negapatnam). Also references a Jaffna detachment with 13 personnel, primarily soldiers from various European cities. Typical of VOC military administration documenting diverse multinational workforce in Ceylon.
